4. Financing terms make a big difference to equity returns. The same contract funded at IG-style spreads, rather than the wider levels on recent facilities, moves equity IRR from about 15% to about 25%.
Caveats: this is one stylised contract, not the company. The capex per MW for new generations is an estimate. And the tax and debt-draw treatment are simplified.

evidence.quote: 2. The real security debate is not lattices vs. hashes — it is lattices vs. building everything on SNARK recursion. That’s because “hash-only” is not really hash-only: it rests on hashes plus the soundness of deep SNARK recursion. Ethereum’s roadmap relies on exactly that: hash-based aggregation needs recursion to keep up with a slot’s worth of signatures,

Here is the (apparently) controversial take I am sticking to: Conditioned on agility, whenever lattices make systems simpler or more functional, we should embrace them rather than default to “hash-only” designs. Lattices are what the rest of the world will depend on, with decades of study and hardening behind them, and at the system level, less functional
Post AGI cryptography: lattice vs hashes.
